title: The Effects of Menstrual Cycle Phase on Exercise Performance in Eumenorrheic Women: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
claims: The review included 78 studies, with 51 eligible for the initial pairwise meta-analysis and 73 for the network meta-analysis.
The overall effect of menstrual cycle phase on exercise performance was trivial, with a median pooled effect size of -0.06 (95% credible interval -0.16 to 0.04).
The largest effect was between the early follicular and late follicular phases (effect size -0.14, 95% credible interval -0.26 to -0.03).
The early follicular phase had the lowest ranking for performance, with a 30% probability of being among the poorest phases, compared with 53% to 55% for other phases.
The quality of evidence was classified as low in 42% of cases, and the authors state that general guidelines across the menstrual cycle cannot be formed.
The authors recommend a personalised approach based on each individual's response across the cycle.
